answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a orchard as the anchor of the cost.
